dedupe_keys.name: gnss jamming and spoofing detection with low cost cots receivers using carrier to noise ratio and calibrated received power

description: This paper presents a methodology to detect and classify radio frequency interference events with low-cost commercial GNSS receivers. It combines carrier-to-noise ratio measurements with a calibrated received power metric to build a two-dimensional detection space that separates nominal, jammed, spoofed and blocked signal conditions. The method is validated with controlled jamming tests in Norway and real-world deployments in Poland and the Southeast Mediterranean, areas that have experienced such interference, and the authors conclude that properly calibrated COTS receivers offer a viable and effective monitoring approach. Producer: Argyris Kriezis and four co-authors; first submitted 17 September 2025, second version 17 July 2026. Coverage: test and deployment sites in Norway, Poland and the Southeast Mediterranean. Access: paper on arXiv; no code or data link was read on the abstract page. Licence and cost: free to read; licence arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence (the paper; no open reuse licence). Caveats: only the abstract page was read, and calibration is required per receiver. Simulation uses: the detection space and thresholds support interference-monitoring design and scenario models of jamming exposure. Related records: GPSJam (data-gpsjam-gnss-interference) and the Estonian GNSS interference series (data-estonian-gnss-interference-narva-tallinn-series).
